A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenRecal and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably, including Appendices A–E and v4's additional Appendices F–J.

before.justification: v3 reports original GenRecal benchmark evaluations, distillation experiments, component ablations, and training/data analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds checkpoint, regularization-form, error/calibration, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The architecture and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. However, new Table 9 lists 'Recalibrator + Student' as trainable during Stage 2, whereas Figure 3(b) and Algorithm 3 in both versions indicate a frozen Recalibrator and trainable student body. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents a procedure change or an erroneous summary.

E1.justification: The training corpus, represented domains, and benchmark/task coverage are retained. Appendix I pools MathVista, MM-Vet, MMMU, and AI2D, all already evaluated in v3. Newly disclosed teacher-response collection is described as applying to all experiments, not as added coverage.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds SFT-only as an explicit comparator to the retained data-scale study, unlike v3 Table 6(d). The named distillation baseline set is unchanged; Table 15 reports computational comparisons for methods already compared in Table 4.

E3.justification: v4 adds intermediate-checkpoint evaluations, alternative regularization controls, and pooled error/calibration evaluation using error categories, JSD, ECE, and wrong-answer confidence. Table 10 also describes random approximately 70% Stage 3 subsampling, conflicting with the VQA-removal procedure retained in Section 4.1(c). This is a changed protocol description, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds evidence separating Stage 2 gains from final SFT; Appendix H tests feature-MSE, KL-only, and CE-only regularization; Appendix I analyzes error structure and calibration. These substantially extend the analyses. Appendix G's component table consolidates existing ablations rather than introducing new ones.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added ECE and wrong-answer confidence values evaluate predictive calibration rather than uncertainty in the reported experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New entries include Stage 2's 74.3 average in Table 9, regularization alternatives scoring 71.7/73.5/74.6 in Table 13, error/calibration outcomes in Table 14, and baseline FLOPs/timings in Table 15. Several other added tables redisplay existing results, so they do not establish improved performance over v3.

T1.justification: Table 13 newly specifies a squared feature-distance objective for the alternative MSE regularizer. The original Equations (1)–(2) and default loss formulations remain unchanged; no new proofs or formal guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The central cross-tokenizer distillation and performance claims remain. Section 4.4 and Appendix F explicitly restrict general-purpose applicability to open-weight teachers, while the rewritten conclusion adds that gains arise primarily from recalibration rather than the multi-stage recipe.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of nonlinear hidden-state alignment, teacher-head regularization versus feature matching, and gains beyond SFT or data scale. Appendix F states the closed/API-teacher limitation and SFT fallback; Appendix I interprets the results as transferring teacher error structure and calibration.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly discloses collecting correct teacher responses with more detailed reasoning before training. Appendix J adds baseline stage/data budgets, optimization comparability, and FLOPs/timing conventions. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and batch settings remain documented as before.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds discussion and citations covering newer VLM training, distillation, pruning, and agent work. Section 4.4 positions novelty in the stable teacher-head distillation recipe, and the acknowledgements identify X-Token as follow-up work. Publication updates to existing references are not new research additions.

P1.justification: v4 extensively edits existing related-work, implementation, and validation paragraphs, condenses and reorganizes Section 4.4, and rewrites the conclusion. It also expands Appendix C, introduces Appendices F–J, revises the Section 3.1 heading, and updates author information.

P2.justification: Tables 8–15 substantially expand the presentation with decomposition, checkpoint, data-budget, consolidated-ablation, calibration, and compute displays; several reorganize existing results. Figures 4–5 are enlarged and the author block is reformatted. Existing figures and Tables 1–7 are retained.

improvement.justification: The added checkpoint and regularization evidence, explicit teacher-access limitation, and training disclosures improve interpretability. However, Table 9 conflicts with the retained Stage 2 freezing scheme, and Table 10 conflicts with the retained Stage 3 data-selection description. These unresolved inconsistencies concern the procedure underlying the results, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality improvement.
